reconstructed_theorem_text: Let iota be finite and let State be its real Euclidean space. Let mu be a probability measure and pi a reference measure, with mu sigma-finite and with the Radon--Nikodym/Lebesgue-decomposition interface. Let L be a real-linear generator and C a real constant. Assume pi satisfies the density-form generator log-Sobolev inequality with multiplier C. Assume the canonical density rho=dmu/dpi is admissible for that LSI, the canonical log-density has an almost-everywhere differentiable score of finite squared integral under mu, the density/log-density pair lies in the required generator integration-by-parts domain, and the carre-du-champ equals rho times the squared score almost everywhere. Then the ENNReal Kullback--Leibler divergence klDiv(mu||pi) is not infinity and its real value is at most (C/2) times the canonical relative Fisher information. The statement does not assert that any concrete pi satisfies LSI or any transport inequality.
